prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on the web search results, I found several recent studies that directly measure the rate at which Large Language Models (LLMs) fabricate citations.

Here are the relevant studies and their reported fabrication rates:

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Of the 222 works cited in the GPT-3.5 papers, 55% are fabricated." | CLAIM: This shows that 55% of citations generated by GPT-3.5 in this study were fabricated.

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Unlike the GPT-3.5 citations, most of the GPT-4 citations refer to works that are verifiably real. Only 18% are fabricated." | CLAIM: This shows that the citation fabrication rate for GPT-4 was a much lower 18%.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Across the 6 reviews, GPT-4o generated 176 citations; 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: This shows that GPT-4o fabricated 19.9% of the citations in a study focused on mental health topics.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Fabrication rates differed significantly by disorder... with higher rates for binge eating disorder (17/60, 28%) and body dysmorphic disorder (14/48, 29%) than for major depressive disorder (4/68, 6%)." | CLAIM: This shows that citation fabrication rates can vary significantly based on the topic, ranging from 6% to 29% for different mental health disorders.

SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%) and are strongly shaped by model, domain, and prompt framing." | CLAIM: This audit of 10 LLMs found that citation fabrication ("hallucination") rates vary widely, from 11.4% to 56.8%.

SOURCE: https://preprints.jmir.org/preprint/80371 | QUOTE: "Thirty-five (19.9%) of the 176 citations were fabricated." | CLAIM: This preprint (which corresponds to the final published paper cited above) confirms the GPT-4o fabrication rate of 19.9%.

SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Our manual verification process identified eight instances of fabricated references." | CLAIM: This study, which analyzed references in published papers, found evidence that a small number of fabricated citations have made it into the peer-reviewed literature, though the overall rate is low. The study does not provide a single percentage fabrication rate for LLM outputs like the others, but rather demonstrates the real-world consequence of the issue.
